rationale: Took the step the last interpretation said was needed: the sweep now emits the operands of each rejected apply, so a receipt can carry the entry that produced it instead of only a count. The draft-side run names the rejected entry exactly, and it is the same entry in all three occurrences - index 4, term 2, one change, JointImplicit - rejected by three different nodes (3, 1 and 4) at the same seed (seed 35, steps 22, 23 and 31), each time with the node reporting applied=4, committed=4, joint_now=true. That is a sharper picture than the count alone: the entry that trips the Changer is a joint-entering change at a single index that several nodes apply, so the shape is not about one lagging node receiving an out-of-order change but about one log position whose content is applied while the tracker is joint. I am not interpreting it further this turn because the operands come from a draft-side run; the experiment below requests isolated execution of these bytes so the same three events with their operands are receipt-backed, and the entry-order question (whether a leave entry should have preceded index 4 and whether the proposer was entitled to append it) becomes answerable from the receipt plus the log state the harness can print next.

scope.description: Twelfth revision of the same fixed harness; probes A-C and the deterministic joint-change case are unchanged. The sweep keeps configuration targets drawn from the joining node or an existing non-leader member, application lag, joint transitions, restarts, the liveness witness and the recovered apply guard, and now additionally emits up to three invalid_change_apply CA_EVENT lines carrying the operands of each rejection: seed, step, node, entry index and term, number of changes, whether the entry requested a joint transition, the node's applied and committed indexes and whether its tracker was joint at that moment. invariant_sweep_summary still reports the counters, including invalid_change_applies and invalid_change_reasons.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, hasUnappliedConfChanges, promotable, newRaft, SetHardState); no production logic is modified.

The operands describe the entry and the node state at the moment of rejection; they do not by themselves establish whether the proposer was entitled to append that entry, which needs the surrounding log.
The event is emitted only for the first three occurrences to bound output; the counter counts all of them.
Randomness is fixed per seed; counts are descriptive, not rates.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup, MsgProp, tick(), isolate, recover, TransferLeader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change, target drawn from node 4 or a non-leader member, half the time JointImplicit), a restart of a random node, or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 (skipping one node about one time in six; applying committed conf changes under recover, and for the first three rejections emitting invalid_change_apply with seed, step, node, entry index, entry term, change count, joint-transition flag, applied, committed and joint_now), then evaluate the four invariants and the liveness witness, finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and sweep case as the previous execution, with the rejection operands instrumented: up to three invalid_change_apply events now carry the entry (index, term, change count, joint flag) and the node state (applied, committed, joint_now) at each rejection. A draft-side run reported the same entry - index 4, term 2, one change, JointImplicit - rejected by nodes 3, 1 and 4 at seed 35 steps 22, 23 and 31, with applied=committed=4 and joint_now=true in all three, which is construction feedback only and is why isolated execution is requested.
